prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System: advisory WUI decision support; continuity over automation when comms/power/sensors impaired. Caldera Incident Command Portal (Emberhall): triages above-threshold cases; marks radio route impaired on bridge failure (Orion ack); jurisdiction constraints before Drone Pilot Operator briefing; produces Crew Staging Pin (time, accuracy, incident ID) used by Helitack Crew Leader to confirm crew position; promotes accepted fire location to Redtail; assignment packages (objective, validity, acks); flags assignments on Confirmed Ignition State change; extended attack mode preserves aviation decisions; disconnected mode: last-sync marking, cached review, queued updates, no irreversible releases; named accounts, RBAC, MFA; auth outage: expiring signed credentials, later supervisor review. Airspace Restricted State: helitack boundary confirmation before aircraft movement. North/South Lookout Camera Masts: heartbeat/temperature/storage/pointing telemetry; North sends smoke bearing, Thermal Spot Snippet to Orion; South sends bearing, Camera Cleaning Log to Smoke Classifier. Horizon Ridge Drone Dock (Kestrel): Battery Swap Ticket to Drone Pilot Operator; no crew movement authority. Drone Tasking Service: mission status; not flight-release authority; no Marigold lane conflict; validates corridor permit before automated task in degraded comms. Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine (Lantern): traceable recommendations, score not declaration; perimeter, probability bands; applies Ridge Shadow Mask; keeps last approved model, rejects unsigned. Smoke Classifier Module: plume confidence to Lantern; produces Ridge Shadow Mask; never sole aircraft basis; advisory if mast down or low image quality. Human confirmation in every decision. MesoWest Weather Fusion Node (Brindle): Wind Shift Bulletin to Redtail; local cache. VHF Radio Gateway Repeater (Badger): fallback relay; queues acks ≥15 min on backhaul loss. Crewline Mobile Tablet: objectives, hazards, route, rally point; hides expired packages; encrypted update queue (author/device/server times). Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console (Marigold): blocks incomplete releases; Runway Release Note; Suppression Drop Receipt. East/West Retardant Loading Pumps: East sends Retardant Batch Slip to Tanker Base Manager, metered recirculation mode; West shift-change inspection. Security: least privilege; separate admin approval; append-only signed audit, buffered offline; maintenance records before status change; operational records retained per agency incident period, raw sensor data shorter; encryption at

New part:
S211: All operational users shall receive communications training that includes VHF Radio Gateway Repeater failure modes, alternate contact paths, call signs, message brevity, and confirmation readbacks.
S212: Weather training shall explain how the MesoWest Weather Fusion Node supports situational awareness and how operators should treat weather inputs when local observations conflict with displayed values.
S213: Initial qualification shall include supervised console practice, scenario walkthroughs, and a documented check by an instructor who is authorized by the operations lead.
S214: Annual refresher training shall include changes to software screens, revised thresholds, updated contact rosters, seasonal hazard briefings, and lessons learned from prior incidents.
S215: Tabletop exercises shall be conducted before the expected peak fire period and shall test detection triage, command notification, airspace coordination, tanker-base coordination, crew deployment, and public-agency liaison actions.
S216: Live exercises shall be scheduled at least once per season when conditions permit and shall include field crews, aircraft coordination staff, drone operations staff, and command-center personnel.
S217: Exercise controllers shall inject realistic complications such as intermittent network service, obscured camera views, delayed field confirmation, resource conflicts, and conflicting reports from external observers.
S218: Performance measures shall include time from automated detection to human review, time from review to command notification, time to resource assignment, communication completion rate, and accuracy of incident status updates.
S219: Detection quality shall be evaluated using confirmed events, benign smoke sources, weather-related artifacts, and operator notes so that both missed detections and false alarms are visible to program management.
S220: Every false-alarm review shall identify the apparent cause, affected sensors or analytic outputs, operator actions, dispatch consequences, and any recommended tuning or training change.
S221: The review board shall include operations, aviation, field crew, maintenance, and county liaison representatives when the event affected more than one operational function.
S222: Seasonal readiness shall require each active user to demonstrate current proficiency, complete required safety briefings, and acknowledge the current operating procedures before receiving operational access.
S223: Personnel who do not meet proficiency requirements shall complete remedial training and a repeat evaluation before performing unsupervised duties in the Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System.
S224: Deployment governance for the Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System shall be managed as a staged release process that follows completion of seasonal readiness activities.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
